title: Questioning Representational Optimism in Deep Learning: The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis
abstract: arXiv:2505.11581v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Much of the excitement in modern AI is driven by the observation that scaling up existing systems leads to better performance. But does better performance necessarily imply better internal representations? While the representational optimist assumes it must, this position paper challenges that view. We compare neural networks evolved through an open-ended search process to networks trained via conventional stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on the simple task of generating a single image. This minimal setup offers a unique advantage: each hidden neuron's full functional behavior can be easily visualized as an image, thus revealing how the network's output behavior is internally constructed neuron by neuron. The result is striking: while both networks produce the same output behavior, their internal representations differ dramatically. The SGD-trained networks exhibit a form of disorganization that we term fractured entangled rep

translated_title: 质疑深度学习中的表征乐观主义：破碎纠缠表征假说
translated_abstract: 现代人工智能领域令人兴奋的诸多进展，都源于这样一个观察：扩展现有系统的规模能带来更好的性能。但更好的性能是否必然意味着更好的内部表征？表征乐观主义者认为必然如此，而本立场文件对这一观点提出了挑战。我们将通过开放式搜索过程演化而来的神经网络与通过传统随机梯度下降（SGD）训练的神经网络，在生成单张图像这一简单任务上进行了比较。这一极简设置具有独特优势：每个隐藏神经元的完整功能行为都可以轻松地可视化为图像，从而能够揭示网络的输出行为是如何在内部逐个神经元构建起来的。结果令人震惊：尽管两个网络产生了相同的输出行为，但它们的内部表征却截然不同。经SGD训练的网络呈现出一种无序状态，我们将其称为“破碎纠缠表征”（fractured entangled representation）……
tldr: 本文通过对比演化网络与SGD训练网络在单图像生成任务上的内部表征，发现两者虽输出行为相同但内部结构截然不同——SGD训练的网络呈现“破碎纠缠表征”，从而挑战了“性能更好必然意味着内部表征更好”的表征乐观主义观点。
en_tdlr: By comparing evolved networks with SGD-trained networks on a single-image generation task, this paper reveals that despite identical output behavior, SGD-trained networks exhibit "fractured entangled representations," challenging the representational optimist assumption that better performance necessarily implies better internal representations.
